findings.title: Inner fastening carries a public, steady declaration
findings.claim: The fastening of the youths' hearts becomes a stable inward axis that carries their rising into public speech, while later changes in bodily and solar orientation make the preserved inner alignment newly perceptible.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers رَبَطْنَا, قُلُوبِهِمْ, قَامُوا۟, قَالُوا۟, and قُلْنَا form a sequence from inward fastening through standing to voiced testimony. The supplied 18:17-18 retrospective and the wider heart-fastening, steadfastness, and standing connections independently return to that sequence; the later Moses scenes supply a contrasting speech register.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees courage as a relation between inward stabilization, visible rising, and speech that remains aligned when surrounding orientation changes.
findings.containment: The ayah's plain account of divine heart-strengthening and the youths' declaration remains intact. This does not claim a universal psychology of courage, that every later speech is reactive, or that the youths' inner alignment never changes; the added relation is a qualified global resonance.

epistemic.reason: The direct cross-run record is trusted and exactly anchored, while the reader-walk and retrospective supports are legacy_unbound; the target connections supply Arabic but not full target morphology, so the integrated relation remains qualified.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişinin yüreği korku anında güçlü ve kararlı kalır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus form رَبَطْنَا carries the fastening that makes the youths' inner resolve hold under threat.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The heart-fastening scenes at 28:10 and 8:11, together with the later 18:17-18 turning image, provide independent pressure and changing-orientation contacts.
branch_activations.activation: The focus fastening meets wider scenes where binding the heart preserves conduct and meets the later contrast between moving bodies and a held inward axis.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Divine fastening is newly legible as the stable inward condition that lets a threatened public declaration proceed.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a bounded relation of firmness and conduct; it does not assert a complete psychological account or eliminate fear.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel anlam, insan ve başka canlılarda bulunan yürek organıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus occurrence قُلُوبِهِمْ supplies the bodily heart as the locus on which fastening acts.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The wider heart-fastening scene and the later moving-body contrast return the focus through the heart as the inward locus of maintained alignment.
branch_activations.activation: The bodily heart carrier contacts the later image of orientation changing outside while the secured inward center remains the point of continuity.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The heart is not only named as an organ; within this bounded resonance it becomes the held center from which public steadiness is possible.
branch_activations.boundary: The packet does not make the organ a literal mechanical anchor or claim that all heart language denotes this inner-center relation.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişi belirli bir işe kesin niyetle yönelir, işi üstlenir ve ona girişir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus form قَامُوا۟ carries the youths' completed rising before their speech.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 46:13 and 11:112 connect the declaration of the Lord with remaining upright and standing as commanded.
branch_activations.activation: The physical rising meets wider standing-and-steadfastness scenes, so the act also becomes an undertaken commitment that issues into testimony.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Their rising is newly perceptible as a deliberate entry into the matter they are about to declare, not only a change of posture.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus still describes a bodily-public rising; no abstract intention is substituted for that action.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus forms قَالُوا۟ and قُلْنَا carry the voiced declaration and its hypothetical self-assessment.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 18:13 truth context, the direct Lord-confession at 46:13, and the later Moses speech scenes provide independent contacts for truthful and reactive public utterance.
branch_activations.activation: The saying words occur after fastening and rising, and their later contrast with reactive speech makes the sequence a relation between inward steadiness and outward testimony.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The youths' words become newly legible as embodied public testimony, not merely a proposition detached from the stabilized act that carries it.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not declare every later speech reactive or prove that bodily stabilization guarantees truth in every speaker.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir nesneyi yüzünden başka yüze çevirmek, ters çevirmek veya altüst etmektir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus heart word carries the q-l-b turning field as a possible secondary contact for the later changes of side and bodily orientation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 18:17-18 retrospective explicitly describes the sun and bodies turning across changing sides.
branch_activations.activation: The later turning image returns through the focus heart carrier and sets external reorientation against the inward faculty that remains fastened.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The declaration is newly seen against a world in which visible orientation can turn without requiring the inner commitment to change with it.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus heart is not redefined as a turning object, and the packet does not claim that inward commitment is incapable of change.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Düşman sınırında yer tutulur, gözetim sürdürülür ve karşı koymaya hazır kalınır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus fastening form carries a possible readiness-to-hold line beyond the immediate emotional firmness.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 8:60 supplies the ribat/preparation contact and 3:200 supplies the wider command of sustained readiness.
branch_activations.activation: The defensive readiness field touches the heart-fastening carrier, making inner firmness also readable as maintained watchfulness before a threatened encounter.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The youths' steadfastness gains a bounded readiness image: they hold their line long enough to speak.
branch_activations.boundary: This is not a military reading of the scene and does not transfer the full border-watch context to the focus.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: düzgünlük, denge ve doğru yoldan sapmama
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şey fiziksel, davranışsal veya yargısal olarak düz çizgisini korur, dengeli olur ve sapmaz.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus rising form carries the physical standing from which a straight-course relation can be contacted.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied istikamah connections at 11:112 and 46:13 return standing and Lord-confession to an undivided course.
branch_activations.activation: The public rising meets the wider straight-course image, so the action can be perceived as keeping a line rather than merely occupying vertical space.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Standing before speech becomes a visible form of remaining aligned with the declaration.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch adds a qualified resonance to the completed rising; it does not replace the physical-public sense with an imperative.

findings.title: Cosmic lordship makes invocation a bounded declaration
findings.claim: The paired Rabb claim, extended over the heavens and the earth, makes the refusal of another ilah a declaration of exclusive authority; the final shatat names rival invocation as speech that crosses the truthful boundary.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers رَبُّنَا, رَبُّ, مِنْ دُونِهِ, إِلَٰهًا, قُلْنَا, and شَطَطًا meet wider declarations of the Lord of the heavens and earth, refusal of another deity, and warnings against shatat. The repeated contacts change the closing speech from a private confession into a bounded public rule for whom one invokes and how one speaks about divine authority.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader perceives both poles of the statement at once: cosmic scope gives the confession its reach, while the final word disciplines speech that would cross that scope into rival attribution.
findings.containment: The focus's ordinary cosmic merism and explicit refusal remain primary. The branch contacts do not claim that every use of Rabb, dūn, ilāh, or shatat carries this full relation, nor that all non-monotheistic speech is thereby classified.

epistemic.reason: The connection rows supply exact target Arabic and direct discovery notes, while target morphology and lexical analysis are not supplied; the branch activations therefore remain bounded global resonances rather than unqualified lexical conclusions.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Sahiplik, buyruk yetkisi ve yönetip düzenleme aynı çekirdekte birleşir.
branch_activations.carrier: The two focus Rabb forms carry personal possession and the following cosmic predicate of lordship.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 7:140 and 26:213 return the Lord claim alongside rejection of rival deities and therefore supply an external authority boundary.
branch_activations.activation: The focus's personal Rabb claim meets wider exclusive-lordship declarations, making the heavens-and-earth predicate a scope for authority rather than decorative breadth.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Rabbuna is newly perceptible as a claim about who governs the whole field in which invocation occurs.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not erase the ordinary possessive address or turn every Rabb occurrence into a universal political claim.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus indefinite ilāhan carries the denied object of invocation and worship.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The wider rows repeatedly refuse seeking or invoking an ilah beside Allah and distinguish the rival object from the one Lord.
branch_activations.activation: The focus object word contacts explicit rival-deity refusals, so the negated invocation is understood as a boundary around worship rather than a generic refusal of any request.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Another ilah is newly visible as a rival worship-object whose admission would alter the declared authority field.
branch_activations.boundary: The packet does not claim that every use of ilah is polemical or that the focus names a complete theology of all worship language.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: başkası ya da daha aşağıda olan
branch_activations.facet_statement: Belirli bir yapıda anılan kişi veya varlığın dışında kalan başkası gösterilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The min dūnihi phrase carries the structural exclusion of an outside alternative.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 26:213 and 40:74 return to the same outside-or-beside relation while rejecting rival invocation.
branch_activations.activation: The besides-word meets explicit external refusals, making the phrase a relational boundary rather than an unqualified spatial lower-position image.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The youths' refusal defines not only whom they name but also the excluded position from which a rival would be invoked.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus phrase is not reduced to a metaphysical ranking of every other thing; the retained relation is the invocation context.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek anlam, gerçek olmayan sözü söyleme veya yükleme işlemidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The final qulnā form carries the speech that the youths hypothetically judge.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The adjacent shatat verdict and 72:4's exact parallel of attributing shatat to speech provide the independent truth-boundary contact.
branch_activations.activation: The speech carrier meets the shatat trigger, allowing the hypothetical consequence to be heard as false or excessive attribution rather than mere vocal excess.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The youths bind their public confession to an epistemic limit: speech that assigns rival authority would become a false claim.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus q-w-l forms are not reclassified as lies in themselves; the false-speech branch is conditional and activated through shatat.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir dava veya hükümde adil çizgiden sapıp bir tarafın aleyhine haksız davranmaktır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus shatatan noun carries the final verdict on the proposed speech.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 72:4 repeats shatat as speech about Allah, while 38:22 places the same root against judging by the truth and not crossing the proper line.
branch_activations.activation: The wider truth-and-boundary contacts make the final noun a judgment on deviation from the proper line, not only a vague intensifier.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The rival invocation is newly framed as speech that departs from the truth-boundary governing the confession.
branch_activations.boundary: Only the contextual boundary facet is retained here; no legal judgment or claim about every excess use is imported.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Gerçekten uzaklaşmış ve doğru sınırını aşmış bir söz söylemektir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus shatatan noun carries the speech-specific form of the boundary verdict.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus qulnā carrier and the wider 72:4 and 38:22 speech-boundary contacts identify shatat as a statement that has crossed truth or measure.
branch_activations.activation: The final verdict contacts both the speech word and its wider parallels, turning the conditional warning into an explicit limit on what may be said about divine authority.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The declaration is not only exclusive in object; it is also disciplined in wording, since a rival attribution would be speech beyond the proper boundary.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not claim that every disagreement is shatat or that the focus's primary translation is displaced by the contextual branch.

friction_notes: All eight HFT records were visible and reviewed, but each supplied zero anchor evidence and no exact context ayah, word index, root, attributed role, or focus-return trace; they were rejected for the missing activation edge, not merely for legacy provenance.

Connection rows provide exact target Arabic and discovery notes but do not supply target-side morphology or lexical analysis, so connection-driven global readings remain qualified and do not inherit retrieval labels as decisions.
The accepted composite preserves the trusted finding together with its legacy reader-walk and retrospective contacts; these sources remain qualified without ranking one reading over another.

No available branch was promoted without a landed focus carrier, independent trigger, changed reading, reader payoff, and explicit boundary; the retained q-l-b, q-w-m, q-w-l, r-b-ṭ, r-b-b, d-w-n, ilah, and shatat contacts are bounded to the relations stated above.
